_comment: The REVIEWED set of divergent shadow pairs ('winner → later divergent claimer') over the catalog corpus — the hard gate of shadow-matrix.test.ts (A1/PAR-11; hardened per the 2026-07-03 review, M2: the snapshot form was silently absorbable by `vitest -u`). Every pair here was inspected and is intentional (a more-specific rule deliberately running before a coarser sibling that reads the same words differently). A NEW pair failing the gate means a rule edit created a fresh divergence: inspect it, fix the ordering/regex if it's a real shadow, or — only after review — add it here with the reason understood. A pair that DISAPPEARS is equally meaningful and must be removed here in the same commit, naming the ADR: 'measureAngle → angle' was dropped by ADR-498 (#969). It had been the bug's own fingerprint sitting in this list as approved — on «זווית ABC = 2α» the numeric rule diverged by reading the coefficient 2 as the degree value, which is exactly the honesty breach #969 reported; `angle` now recognises a symbolic value and refuses it, so the divergence no longer exists. A shadow that is a WRONG reading is not made safe by being shadowed — rule order was the only thing hiding it. 'lineCutsCircleTwice → lineLineIntersection' was dropped by ADR-531 (#1274) on 2026-09-20: on «the line AO cuts circle O at C and D» (and its Hebrew twin) the coarser crossing rule used to claim the sentence with carriers that share a letter, which the operator's coincidence ruling now refuses by name — so it returns a clarify instead of an array and stops diverging. The WINNER is unchanged (lineCutsCircleTwice, per the snapshot that still passes), and lineLineIntersection still diverges elsewhere ('circumcircleMeetsSegment → lineLineIntersection' stands), so the rule did not go silent — it stopped mis-reading one shape. 'circumcircle → circle' was dropped by ADR-548 (#1438) on 2026-09-27: on «circle through A B C» the `circle` rule used to diverge by reading only the FIRST through-label (a circle through A, B and C dropped) — the uppercase-residue hole #1438 closed. A definition now lowers exactly one through point and fails closed on a longer list, so it no longer claims the 3-point sentence; the circumcircle winner is unchanged. '(anon)' entries are unnamed arrow-function rules (position-stable). 'roleLength → segment' and 'roleLength → distanceConstraint' were added by ADR-574 (#1607, round #1736) on 2026-10-04: on «האלכסון AC = 8» / "the diagonal AC is 8" the composer is the more-specific rule by construction — its output is the role rule's own reading PLUS the length lane's (it calls both through parse()), so each later claimer diverges by emitting a strict SUBSET: segment keeps the diagonal and drops the 8 (the #1607 defect itself, which the honesty gate refused), distanceConstraint keeps the 8 and drops the diagonal claim (ADR-499). Neither is a correct reading the composer hides; the compoundAtDistance → pointOnSegment shape. 'semicircle → diameterFromPoint' and 'semicircle → circumcircle' were added by ADR-589 (#1771, round #1776) on 2026-10-05: on the new catalog spelling «חצי מעגל שקוטרו AB העובר דרך C» / "semicircle with diameter AB through C" the semicircle rule is the more-specific reading by construction (a 180° arc on AB with C ON it); the coarser FULL-circle rules read the same words as a whole circle (circumcircle: a circle through the labels; diameterFromPoint: a diameter-led circle). Neither is the sentence's meaning, and the semicircle rule already ran before both. The same utterance also diverges against circleOnDiameter (already listed), whose reading drops «העובר דרך C» outright — that is #1795's defect, not a correct reading this shadow hides.
